_comment: Conventional Commits → a version bump, a tag, and a GitHub Release.
── One package, one version
This repository ships the `gist` binary, `libgist` + include/gist.h, and
the Python and Rust bindings over them. They are released together, so
they carry one number, and `build.zig.zon`'s `.version` is where that
number is written. `src/root.zig` reads it through a build option (so
`gist --version`, `--schema`, and the generated man page answer with it),
Rust reads CARGO_PKG_VERSION, and Python reads its installed distribution
metadata. Only the two publishing manifests restate it, below.
── This is NOT the engine's version
`irregex` versions on its own schedule and is pinned as a dependency, not
mirrored here. `gist rg --pcre2-version` and the engine's own accessor are
how you ask about what is underneath.
── Why `simple` + generic extra-files
There is no Zig updater. `simple` keeps the manifest as the source of
truth and the `generic` updater rewrites the semver on any line carrying
an `x-release-please-version` annotation, so one release moves every
member of the lockstep atomically. `tools/version_parity.py` fails if a
marked line is missing from this list, so the two cannot drift apart.
── Changelog ownership
towncrier owns CHANGELOG.md — the curated fragments under changelog.d/ are
the release notes, written for people. release-please would compile a
second, machine-derived changelog into the same file and fight it, so
`skip-changelog` is on and the bot handles versions and tags only. The
`fold changelog` job in release-please.yml builds the notes and commits
them onto this PR's branch automatically; release.yml's preflight
re-checks that the fold landed before it will publish anything.
── What picks the number
The stock `default` strategy, unmodified: a `!` or a BREAKING CHANGE
footer takes the major, `feat` takes the minor, and everything else takes
the patch. `bump-minor-pre-major` and `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major`
used to sit below and are gone — release-please reads them only while the
version is under 1.0.0, so they went inert when this package shipped
1.0.0 and stayed on reading like a policy nobody consults. The full table,
the 0.x variant, and the `Release-As: X.Y.Z` override that pins an exact
version live in the org standard:
https://github.com/The-Billy-Company/.github/blob/main/RELEASING.md#what-picks-the-number
── No `package-name`
It used to say `gist-search`, and that one line is why the bot has never cut
a release here. With the component out of the tag, release-please writes the
release PR's body with no component and names its branch
`release-please--branches--main` with no component either; but the guard it
then runs over a merged standalone PR compares that empty component against
`component || package-name`. A name here makes those two halves of its own
bookkeeping disagree permanently, so every merge logged `PR component:
undefined does not match configured component: gist-search` and returned
without tagging — which then reads as an untagged merged release PR and
wedges the NEXT run too. The name buys nothing back: with
`include-component-in-tag` false, the tag is `vX.Y.Z` and the release is
titled `vX.Y.Z` whatever the package is called. It is why main has said
1.2.0 since August with `v1.1.0` still the newest tag.
── `always-update`
The `fold changelog` job deletes the fragments it folded, on the release
PR's branch. So as soon as a commit on main edits one of those files, the
branch and its base disagree modify/delete — and GitHub cannot compute a
merge ref for a conflicting PR, so no `pull_request` workflow runs at all,
`release-ready` never appears, and the PR sits unmergeable behind a
checklist of nothing. Default release-please rebuilds the branch only when
the release notes change, which makes precisely the wrong pushes invisible
to it: a `ci`/`docs`/`chore` commit carrying a fragment writes no note. This
is upstream's knob for "pull requests must not be out-of-date with the base
branch", and it costs a rebuilt branch on every push while a PR is open —
which is why the fold recomputes from main rather than appending, and
cancels a superseded run of itself rather than queuing behind one.
── The tag cascades
Merging the release PR tags `vX.Y.Z`, which is what `release.yml` waits
for to publish the wheels. A tag pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN does NOT trigger
another workflow, so that hand-off only happens because release-please runs
as the `billy-company-release` GitHub App rather than as Actions — see
.github/workflows/release-please.yml.
